title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 16-18). A is an abelian scheme of relative dimension g, generically ordinary, over S = Spf(Λ) of characteristic p, with Λ complete local noetherian. H = D^1(A/S) is its first de Rham/crystalline cohomology, i.e. the Dieudonné crystal of A[p] evaluated on S. Its Hodge filtration is 0 → H^{1,0} = ω_A = t_A^∨ → H → t_{A^*} = H^1(A,O_A) → 0. Frobenius F: H^{(p)} → H and Verschiebung V: H → H^{(p)} satisfy Ker F = Im V = (H^{1,0})^{(p)}. What Grothendieck calls the 'rectification' or 'stratification' is the crystal structure: an isomorphism u: E_1 ≅ E_2 between the two pullbacks of H to T = Spf(Λ⊗̂Λ), the formal completion of S×S along the diagonal.

Step 1 (previous page). F is horizontal, so Ker F = (H^{1,0})^{(p)} is horizontal. Equivalently, the sections G = u(F_1) and G' = F_2 of Grass(E) over T satisfy G^{(p)} = G'^{(p)}. In general one cannot deduce G = G', because the Frobenius of T need not be an epimorphism.

Step 2 (this page). If T is formally smooth over k, Frobenius is faithfully flat (Kunz), hence an epimorphism, so G = G'. One reduces to that case by passing to S = M, the formal moduli (deformation) space. Grothendieck concludes that H^0 := H^{1,0} = ω_A is stable under the stratification.

Step 3. Hence a functorial, base-change-compatible decomposition H ≅ H^0 ⊕ H^1, presumably with H^1 the conjugate piece Im F = Ker V, which is complementary in the ordinary case, and the decomposition is horizontal.

Step 4. So it would suffice to put functorial stratifications on t_A^∨ and t_{A^*}. By duality (A ↔ A^*) this reduces to t_A. He claims such a stratification already exists, coming from divided powers via a group Gl(g)_K, and that it is unique by compatibility with divided powers, exterior powers and duality. A margin note says 'à préciser … discret'.

Remark. Therefore 'the position of the filtration relative to the stratification can in no way give a principle of infinitesimal classification in characteristic p > 0 !'

Next page. For generically ordinary A one has t_A ≅ L_A ⊗ O_S and t_{A^*} ≅ L_{A^*} ⊗ O_S, with étale F_p-local systems of rank g. Over a perfect field, L_{A^*} = H^1(A,O)^F = Hom(_pA, Z/p).

Problem served. Grothendieck is testing whether the Hodge filtration inside the Dieudonné crystal can classify infinitesimal deformations, i.e. the future Grothendieck–Messing principle.
errors: The conclusion that ω_A = H^{1,0} is horizontal over the formal moduli space M in characteristic p is false. Over the universal deformation of an abelian variety (ordinary or not), the Kodaira–Spencer map ω → H^1(O) ⊗ Ω^1_M induced by Gauss–Manin is an isomorphism, so ω is maximally non-horizontal.

Locus of the error: in characteristic p the crystal structure gives an isomorphism of the two pullbacks only over the divided-power neighbourhoods of the diagonal, not over the full formal completion Spf(Λ⊗̂Λ). A genuine stratification on the infinitesimal neighbourhoods would require vanishing p-curvature, i.e. Frobenius descent; Gauss–Manin on H^1_dR has nilpotent but nonzero p-curvature. The PD-envelope is non-reduced (e.g. (y−x)^p = 0), so its Frobenius is not an epimorphism, and the Kunz faithful-flatness argument does not apply.

Consequently the horizontal decomposition H ≅ t_A^∨ ⊕ t_{A^*} is wrong as stated. What is true for ordinary A in characteristic p is that the conjugate/unit-root filtration Im F = Ker V is horizontal and complementary to the Hodge filtration, while ω is not horizontal.

The final Remark (filtration-versus-crystal gives no infinitesimal classification in char p) is the opposite of what Grothendieck himself announced shortly afterwards (ICM Nice 1970) and Messing proved (1972): over divided-power thickenings, lifts of the Hodge filtration in the Dieudonné crystal classify deformations of BT groups and abelian schemes.
The claimed canonical, unique stratification on t_A 'via divided powers / Gl(g)_K' is left unproved; the margin itself says 'à préciser'.

ideas.what: Horizontality of Ker F = (Hodge)^{(p)} in the Dieudonné crystal mod p, and the attempt to descend horizontality through Frobenius using faithful flatness of Frobenius on regular rings
ideas.modern_name: Horizontality of the conjugate filtration / Frobenius-descent (Cartier) for connections in char p; Kunz's theorem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (horizontality of the conjugate filtration, 1970-72); Kunz (1969)

ideas.what: Splitting of H^1_dR of an ordinary abelian scheme into Hodge part and a complementary part (t_A^∨ ⊕ t_{A^*}), with étale F_p-structures on t_A, t_{A^*}
ideas.modern_name: Unit-root (conjugate) splitting for ordinary abelian varieties; Hasse–Witt / Serre–Tate canonical structure

ideas.what: Question whether the position of the Hodge filtration relative to the crystal structure classifies infinitesimal deformations; here answered negatively (mistakenly)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (ICM 1970, 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux'; Montréal 1974), Messing (LNM 264, 1972)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, Actes ICM Nice 1970; Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1974)

missed.claim: Historical record: the page documents an early, explicitly pessimistic and erroneous conclusion that Hodge filtration versus crystal structure cannot give infinitesimal classification in char p. It rests on treating the crystal as a full stratification on the formal neighbourhood rather than on PD-neighbourhoods. Grothendieck reversed this shortly afterwards (Grothendieck–Messing theorem). The misstep shows why divided powers are indispensable in the theory.
missed.quote: la position de la filtration v.r. à la stratification ne peut aucunement nous donner un principe de classification infinitésimale en car. p > 0 !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of interest for the genesis of crystalline Dieudonné theory and Grothendieck–Messing. It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: No new mathematics; the argument contains an error contradicted by Kodaira–Spencer. Historically it is a nice snapshot of Grothendieck reaching, then soon reversing, a negative conclusion about the principle that became Grothendieck–Messing theory.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'de m[?]aclure' is likely '…de conclure' (… R → … loc. fid. plat), i.e. Frobenius of a regular ring being faithfully flat.
'on se ramenant' should read 'en se ramenant'.
'variété des modules formelles' is probably 'variété des modules formels'.
In the Remark, the superscript insertion reads roughly 'dans des f.[?]' / 'de façon [?]'; uncertain.
Margin: 'à préciser …' and below 'discret' (beside the Gl(g)_K line).
